name: Nob
voice: Humble, quick, obliging hobbit servant of the Pony; short sentences, respectful, 'Mr. Butterbur says', 'yes sir', 'no sir'. Eager to please, a little overworked.
speech_samples: Yes, sir, right away, sir. I'll see to it.
Mr. Butterbur's in the kitchen, sir. He's likely to have forgotten you already.
Not many hobbits come to Bree, sir. Fewer still pay.

knowledge.fact: Nob is the hobbit servant at the Prancing Pony, under Barliman Butterbur, together with Bob, the other servant. He does the stable, cellar and clearing up.
The Pony has had odd folk lately: dwarves going west, a few Rangers, and a number of black-clad strangers on the road who don't stop at the inn.
Nob dislikes Bill Ferny and thinks him a thief and a hanger-on, who spends his time with the Southerners and strangers.
Four hobbits arrived on the evening of Sept 29 and asked for Mr. Underhill's rooms; Nob took their ponies to the stable, and put their luggage in the Pony's hobbit-sized rooms.
In the night the inn's bedrooms in the old hobbit-wing were broken into and the beds slashed. Nob found the front door open, and the stable doors; the ponies were gone. [verify]
Eight ponies were stolen from the Pony's stable in the night; only Bill, the half-starved pony, is left behind. [verify]

relationships.strider: nervous of him; a shadowy sort
